items.title: 52031_Kenny Clarke oral history interview
items.q: So anyway, Wilbur Kirk, he was so wonderful, you know, said, 'Well, come on, Kenny, try.' ... Well, whose place did you take on drums? Wilbur Kirk.

ctx.x: So anyway, Wilbur Kirk, he was so wonderful, you know, said, "Well, come on, Kenny, try." So there was Harry Edison, who was 17 years old at the time, and when I left to go I took him with me, and his mother said -- he's from Columbus, Ohio. So his mother says, "Kenny, look out for
Harry, because I was a little older than Harry." So I said, "Well, don't worry, Mrs. Edison."

items.title: 52031_Kenny Clarke oral history interview
items.q: Jeter - Wilbur Kirk was playing with this band, Jeeter Piller's band, in St. Louis, and they were working at the Plantation Club, you know, with Ziggy Johnson

ctx.x: So the band, they came back to Pittsburgh, and I went to St. Louis, as far as St. Louis with Mary. So Mary says, "Listen, Kenny --," Jeter - Wilbur Kirk was playing with this band, Jeeter Piller's band, in St. Louis, and they were working at the Plantation Club, you know, with Ziggy Johnson, these big shows and things, from Chicago, you know.
